families.title: Orientable surface
families.description: The closed orientable surface of genus g: one 4g-gon glued by a₁ b₁ a₁⁻¹ b₁⁻¹ ⋯ (genus 0: the sphere as a disc glued by a a⁻¹).

families.title: Non-orientable surface
families.description: The closed surface with k crosscaps: one 2k-gon glued by c₁ c₁ ⋯ c_k c_k (k = 1, the projective plane; k = 2, the Klein bottle).

families.title: Klein bottle
families.description: A square glued by a b a⁻¹ b: one vertex, two edges, one 2-cell.

families.title: Polygons glued by words
families.description: Any polygons, each a word: a lowercase letter is a side along the polygon, its capital a side against it; equal letters are one edge.

families.title: Dunce hat
families.description: A triangle glued by a a a⁻¹: contractible, yet without a free edge, so it does not collapse (Zeeman 1964).

families.title: Sphere
families.description: The n-sphere as a point with one n-cell.

families.title: Real projective space
families.description: ℝPⁿ with one cell in each dimension, ∂e_k = (1 + (−1)^k) e_{k−1}.

families.title: Complex projective space
families.description: ℂPⁿ with one cell in each even dimension.

families.title: Lens space
families.description: L(p, q) with one cell in each dimension, the 2-cell glued by aᵖ: π₁ = ℤ/p.

families.title: Presentation complex
families.description: One vertex, a loop for each letter, a 2-cell for each relator: its π₁ is the presented group. Relators are words, separated by spaces.

families.title: Lattice torus
families.description: The periodic n × m square lattice: the torus as a product of circles, with its links and plaquettes, the arena of lattice gauge theory.

families.title: Lattice disc
families.description: The n × m square grid: a disc, on which the plaquettes of a gauge field are independent and Wilson loops obey an exact area law.

families.title: Lattice cylinder
families.description: A circle of n links times an interval of m: an annulus.

families.title: Lattice 3-torus
families.description: The periodic n × n × n cubic lattice, with its cubes.

families.title: Boundary of a simplex
families.description: ∂Δⁿ, the (n−1)-sphere on n + 1 vertices.

families.title: Octahedron
families.description: The boundary of the cross-polytope: a 2-sphere on 6 vertices.

families.title: Seven-vertex torus
families.description: The minimal triangulation of the torus (Möbius 1886; Császár 1949).

families.title: Six-vertex projective plane
families.description: The minimal triangulation of ℝP², the icosahedron with antipodes identified.

families.title: Suspended 3-sphere
families.description: The suspension of ∂Δ³: a 3-sphere on 6 vertices.

families.title: Simplicial complex from facets
families.description: Any simplicial complex, its facets as lists of vertices separated by semicolons.

families.title: Dual 2-complex of ∂Δⁿ
families.description: The 2-complex dual to the boundary of the n-simplex: a vertex per facet, an edge per ridge, a 2-cell around each codimension-2 face. For n = 4, the spin-foam 2-complex of the 3-sphere.

families.title: Dual of the seven-vertex torus
families.description: The hexagonal torus dual to the minimal triangulation.

families.title: Melonic graph
families.description: A melonic (D+1)-coloured graph: the elementary melon with k melons inserted at random. Its 2-complex is the dual 2-skeleton of a D-sphere; the leading order of a coloured tensor model.

families.title: Random coloured graph
families.description: A random (D+1)-coloured bipartite graph with 2p vertices: a Feynman graph of a group field theory, shown as its 2-complex of bicoloured cycles.

families.title: Pseudomanifold of a coloured graph
families.description: The D-dimensional pseudomanifold a random coloured graph encodes, as a Δ-complex: k-cells are the components of the subgraphs on D − k colours.
